tracks.name: Hub City Dragway
tracks.race_days: None. The track is permanently closed.
tracks.notes:
Hub City Dragway was a quarter-mile asphalt track in Hattiesburg at about 280 feet elevation, running IHRA ET bracket racing on Saturdays with test and tune on Friday and Sunday.

It is permanently closed. We confirmed this directly on 12 September 2026, in a reply from one of the numbers published for the track: the track is closed and the land has been sold. Asked when, the reply was “years ago”. That is a permanent closure, not a pause, and it happened long enough back that the listings still showing it as open have been wrong for a considerable time.

The public record already pointed that way. Google Maps lists the business as permanently closed. Of the four phone numbers published across various listings, two were disconnected, one rang through to voicemail, and the fourth is the one that replied. The most recent social media activity we could find dates to late 2024, and one national track directory had already listed it as closed.

The reason this is worth stating plainly: the track's own website is still online, its Yelp listing was updated in 2026, and its Facebook page still carries 971 reviews. Anyone searching for it would reasonably conclude it is still racing. It is not, and the land it sat on is no longer in racing use.

If you are looking for a track near Hattiesburg, Swamp Bottom Dragstrip in Columbia is about 30 miles away and opened in September 2026.
tracks.caveat: This track is closed and the land has been sold. Its website, Yelp listing and Facebook page are all still up, which is why other directories still list it as operating.
tracks.answer: Hub City Dragway in Hattiesburg, Mississippi is permanently closed. We confirmed this directly with the track in September 2026: the strip has closed and the land has been sold.
faq: Is Hub City Dragway still open?

No. Hub City Dragway in Hattiesburg is permanently closed and the land has been sold. We confirmed this directly with the track in September 2026. Google Maps also lists the business as permanently closed. Its website and social pages are still online, which is why several directories continue to list it as operating.
What happened to the Hub City Dragway property?
The land has been sold. We confirmed this directly with the track on 12 September 2026. We do not know what it will be used for.
When did Hub City Dragway close?

Years ago. That is the answer we got directly from the track when we asked on 12 September 2026. We have not been able to pin down an exact date. The most recent social media activity we can find dates to late 2024, though that may be people posting about the track rather than the track operating. If you know the year it stopped racing, or remember the last race, tell us and we will record it.
What is the closest drag strip to Hattiesburg now?

Swamp Bottom Dragstrip in Columbia, Mississippi, about 30 miles away. It opened on 5 September 2026 and is an NHRA member track in the South Central Division. Gulfport Dragway is about 60 miles from Hattiesburg and races Wednesday nights and weekends year-round.

camping.detail: Unconfirmed, as is the track's operating status.

tracks.name: Swamp Bottom Dragstrip
tracks.race_days: Schedule forming. Sept. 25-26 Run What You Brung weekend announced; future bracket racing has been discussed but no bracket date is confirmed.
tracks.address: Highway 43, south Marion County, Columbia, MS
tracks.notes: Opened September 5–6, 2026. Built on more than 300 acres of former timber land by owners Bradley and Tawan Reid, after about two years of work. Facility includes a quarter-mile concrete surface, viewing tower, grandstands, restrooms and parking. Joined the NHRA Member Track Network in July 2026, which makes it eligible to run the NHRA Summit Racing E.T. Series presented by Hoosier, the Summit Jr. Drag Racing League, NHRA Street Legal and Jr. Street. Opening weekend was deliberately test and tune plus grudge racing, to lay rubber on fresh concrete before points racing begins.
tracks.caveat: No independent website yet. The track's Facebook page is the current source for updates while the schedule develops. Several Sept. 25-26 shootout rules still need official clarification — call ahead before you tow.
tracks.answer: Swamp Bottom Dragstrip is a quarter-mile concrete drag strip in Columbia, Mississippi. It opened on 5 September 2026 and is an NHRA member track in the South Central Division.
faq: When did Swamp Bottom Dragstrip open?

Swamp Bottom Dragstrip held its grand opening weekend on 5 and 6 September 2026. Opening weekend was test and tune plus no-prep grudge racing, run deliberately to lay rubber down on the fresh concrete before points racing begins.
Who owns Swamp Bottom Dragstrip?
Swamp Bottom Dragstrip is owned by Bradley and Tawan Reid, who spent about two years building the facility on more than 300 acres of former timber land.
Is Swamp Bottom Dragstrip an NHRA track?

Yes. Swamp Bottom joined the NHRA Member Track Network in July 2026 as part of the South Central Division, Division 4. That makes it eligible to run the NHRA Summit Racing E.T. Series presented by Hoosier, the Summit Jr. Drag Racing League, NHRA Street Legal and Jr. Street.

camping.detail: Unconfirmed. The facility sits on more than 300 acres and published coverage of the opening lists a concrete track, viewing tower, restrooms, grandstands and parking areas — no camping or RV hookups are mentioned. There are reports of RV pads with electricity but we have not verified them. Call the track and ask.

tracks.name: Gulfport Dragway
tracks.race_days: Wednesday nights plus weekends, January through December. Gates 6pm Wednesdays, weather permitting.
tracks.notes:
The busiest track on the Mississippi Gulf Coast and the anchor of the region. Founded in 1972 as Magnolia Dragway. Runs the Busch Light King of the Mountain series on Wednesdays and an IHRA Track Championship Series on weekends, including the Summer Iron Man Challenge. Hosts the Gulf Coast DragFest and the Southeast Gassers Association Gulf Coast Nationals. Elevation is about 21 feet, the lowest in the region — worth knowing if you are correcting for air density.

On 17 September 2026, Gulfport Dragway announced that the SDPC Raceshop Great American 50Ks was moving from Montgomery to Gulfport for Oct. 13-17, with parking beginning Oct. 12 and four $50,000-to-win race days.

On 18 September 2026, Gulfport announced a late-breaking addition to the 3rd Annual Cruisin' After Dark on Oct. 8: Neil Esposito's Jersey Attitude Jet Dragster. Gates open 5 PM, track hot 6-11 PM, and spectator admission is $10.
tracks.directions: I-10 exit 31, south on Canal Road, cross the railroad tracks about a mile, left onto Racetrack Road.
tracks.answer: Gulfport Dragway is a quarter-mile and eighth-mile asphalt drag strip in Gulfport, Mississippi. It races Wednesday nights and weekends from January through December and is IHRA sanctioned.
faq: What time do gates open at Gulfport Dragway?
Gates open at 6pm on Wednesday nights, weather permitting. Weekend event times vary by event.
How old is Gulfport Dragway?
Gulfport Dragway opened in 1972 as Magnolia Dragway and has been the leading quarter-mile and eighth-mile strip on the Mississippi Gulf Coast for over 30 years.
What is the elevation at Gulfport Dragway?
About 21 feet above sea level, the lowest of any track in this region. That matters if you are correcting for air density when setting a dial-in.

camping.detail: Unconfirmed. The track markets itself as a racecation destination with beaches, restaurants and casinos nearby, but we have not confirmed whether overnight pit parking or hookups are available on site.

tracks.name: Byram Dragway
tracks.race_days: Tuesday Night Midnight Madness — test and tune plus grudge racing. Check the track’s Facebook page for other events.
tracks.notes:
A quarter-mile asphalt track on Siwell Road in Byram, immediately south of Jackson, and the closest strip to the Jackson metro.

It was formerly known as Jackson Dragway and now operates as Byram Dragway. The change is why the track is easy to write off as dead: directory listings under the old name still carry a phone number that is disconnected, Google Maps reviews under the old name stop around 2024, and no current schedule appears under either name outside Facebook. The track itself is running weekly.

The regular programme is Tuesday Night Midnight Madness, billed as test and tune with grudge racing. Gate prices as advertised in September 2026 are $25 for racers and $15 for spectators. The track describes itself as the little track with all the action.

Schedule and event announcements go out through the Facebook page rather than a website, so check there before travelling.
tracks.caveat: This track was previously called Jackson Dragway. Old listings under that name carry a disconnected phone number and stale hours — use the Facebook page for current information.
tracks.answer: Byram Dragway, formerly Jackson Dragway, is a quarter-mile asphalt drag strip at 7557 S Siwell Rd in Byram, Mississippi, just south of Jackson. It runs Tuesday Night Midnight Madness — test and tune and grudge racing — at $25 for racers and $15 for spectators.
faq: Is Jackson Dragway still open?

Yes, but it is now called Byram Dragway. Same location, 7557 S Siwell Rd in Byram, Mississippi. It was confirmed operating on 12 September 2026, running Tuesday Night Midnight Madness. Listings under the old Jackson Dragway name carry a disconnected phone number, which makes the track look closed when it is not.
What is Tuesday Night Midnight Madness at Byram Dragway?
A weekly Tuesday night programme of test and tune plus grudge racing. Advertised gate prices in September 2026 are $25 for racers and $15 for spectators.
Where is Byram Dragway?
7557 S Siwell Rd, Byram, MS 39272, just south of Jackson and about 85 miles from Hattiesburg.

tracks.name: Atmore Dragstrip
tracks.race_days: None. The track is permanently closed.
tracks.notes:
An eighth-mile concrete track at 1301 Racetrack Rd in Atmore, just off I-65 near the Alabama and Florida line, and for years the nearest Alabama option to the Mississippi Gulf Coast.

It is permanently closed. Google lists the business as permanently closed as of 12 September 2026. The listing still carries a 4.5 star rating from 355 reviews and photographs of a packed house, which gives some idea of what the place was when it was running.

It was still listed as a current member track by a national sanctioning body when we compiled this directory, which is worth knowing if you are relying on those lists to plan a weekend. Member track lists record who joined, not who is still racing.

If you are looking for an eighth-mile in that part of Alabama, tell us and we will go find one.
tracks.caveat: This track is closed. It still appears on at least one sanctioning body's member track list, which is how it ended up on this site in the first place.
tracks.answer: Atmore Dragstrip in Atmore, Alabama is permanently closed. Google lists the business as permanently closed, though it still shows a 4.5 rating from 355 reviews from when it was operating.
faq: Is Atmore Dragstrip still open?

No. Atmore Dragstrip in Atmore, Alabama is permanently closed. Google lists the business as permanently closed as of September 2026. It still appears on at least one sanctioning body's member track list, which does not reflect current operating status.
Where was Atmore Dragstrip?
1301 Racetrack Rd, Atmore, AL 36502, just off Interstate 65 near the Alabama and Florida line.

tracks.name: State Capitol Raceway
tracks.race_days: Uncertain. The track announced a lease problem in April 2026 and has not posted a schedule since.
tracks.notes:
A quarter-mile track on Highway 190 in Port Allen, just across the river from Baton Rouge, and historically one of the significant strips in Louisiana. Racers in the comments recall top fuel running here in the Cajun Nationals era.

On 24 April 2026 the track posted an update saying it had been unable to reach an agreement with the owners of the portion of the property it leased, that efforts to find a path forward had not been successful, and that it was actively exploring alternative options to keep racing alive. The post drew over 1,100 reactions, 165 comments and 127 shares.

As of 12 September 2026 there has been no public update since. Google still lists the business normally with a 4.5 rating from 400 reviews and has not marked it closed, but the listing is unclaimed, so Google has no current information from the operator either.

We are not calling this closed. We are saying its future is unresolved and you should not plan a weekend around it without confirming. If you know the current position, tell us.
tracks.caveat: Confirm before travelling. The track has not announced a schedule since April 2026 and its future is unresolved.
tracks.answer: State Capitol Raceway in Port Allen, Louisiana has an uncertain future. In April 2026 the track announced it had been unable to reach an agreement with the owners of leased property and was exploring alternatives to keep racing alive. It has not posted publicly since.
faq: Is State Capitol Raceway still open?

Uncertain. In April 2026 the track announced it had been unable to reach a lease agreement with the property owners and was exploring alternatives to keep racing alive. There has been no public update since. Google has not marked the business closed, but the listing is unclaimed. Confirm before travelling.
What happened to State Capitol Raceway?

The track posted on 24 April 2026 that it could not reach terms with the owners of the leased portion of its property. It said it was actively exploring alternative options to keep racing alive. No further public update has appeared as of September 2026.
Where is State Capitol Raceway?
11436 US-190, Port Allen, LA 70767, just west of Baton Rouge.

tracks.name: No Problem Raceway Park
tracks.race_days: TNT Test ’n Tune on selected Fridays, Bracket Masters on selected Saturdays, plus road course events, Super Saturdays and special races. A monthly calendar is published on Facebook.
tracks.answer: No Problem Raceway Park is an NHRA-sanctioned quarter-mile drag strip at 6470 LA-996 in Belle Rose, Louisiana. The site also carries a 1.8-mile asphalt road course and over 200 acres used for concerts, car shows and festivals.
tracks.notes:
A multi-discipline motorsports facility in Belle Rose, in the Louisiana river parishes between Baton Rouge and Houma. Confirmed active on 12 September 2026. The track is running its 25th anniversary season, having opened in 2001.

The drag strip is a quarter-mile sanctioned by NHRA. Alongside it sits a 1.8-mile asphalt road course and more than 200 acres used for concerts, car shows and festivals. That mix is unusual in this region — most tracks listed here do one thing.

The regular programme runs TNT Test ’n Tune on selected Friday nights and Bracket Masters on selected Saturdays, with road course events, Super Saturdays run with Flip Flop Promotions, and private pro test sessions bookable by phone. The track publishes a calendar of events each month on its Facebook page.

It also hosts the Pure Speed Drag Racing Experience, a ride-and-drive programme for people who want to run a race car without owning one, booked separately from the racing calendar.

Two phone numbers are in use: 225-445-3498 and 985-369-3692. The number printed on the track's own website has an extra digit and cannot be dialled as written.
faq: Is No Problem Raceway an NHRA track?
Yes. The quarter-mile drag strip at No Problem Raceway Park is sanctioned by NHRA. The site also carries a 1.8-mile asphalt road course.
What days does No Problem Raceway race?

TNT Test ’n Tune runs on selected Friday nights and Bracket Masters on selected Saturdays, alongside road course events, Super Saturdays and special races. A calendar of events is published each month on the track's Facebook page.
What else is at No Problem Raceway Park besides the drag strip?
A 1.8-mile asphalt road course and over 200 acres used for concerts, car shows and festivals. It also hosts the Pure Speed Drag Racing Experience, a ride-and-drive programme.
What is the phone number for No Problem Raceway Park?
Two numbers are in use: 225-445-3498 and 985-369-3692. The number printed on the track's own website has an extra digit and cannot be dialled as written.
Where is No Problem Raceway Park?
6470 LA-996, Belle Rose, LA 70341, in the Louisiana river parishes between Baton Rouge and Houma, about 136 miles from Hattiesburg.

camping.detail: Unconfirmed. Worth asking given the size of the site and the festival use.

tracks.name: Twin City Raceway
tracks.race_days: Bracket racing on scheduled Saturdays plus TNT Friday nights. Check the track’s Facebook page for the current calendar.
tracks.notes:
An IHRA member track in Monroe, north Louisiana, running under the House of Hook banner. Confirmed active on 12 September 2026.

The bracket programme runs four classes. As advertised for the September 2026 race, Super Pro pays $5,000 to win with a $125 entry, No Box pays $2,000 with a $90 entry, Street pays $500 with a $40 entry, and Jr Dragster pays $500 with a $40 entry. Runner-up, semi-final and quarter-final money is posted for each class, and buybacks are available. Car counts are capped by class.

Gates typically open at noon with time trials from 1pm. Spectators $15, children $10. TNT sessions run $50 with a diaper required and a TNT stop after the third round of eliminations.

The track also hosts a Gasser Revival. Google lists this track as Twin City Motorsports Park at 3695 Prairie Rd with the number 318-557-3284, while the track's own Facebook page uses Twin City Raceway, gives the address as 3695 Hwy 841 and the number 318-266-7441. Prairie Rd and Highway 841 meet at the property, so both are correct. Use either name when searching.

Schedule announcements go out through Facebook rather than a website, so check there before travelling.
tracks.answer: Twin City Raceway is an IHRA-sanctioned eighth-mile drag strip at 3695 Prairie Rd in Monroe, Louisiana. It runs bracket racing with Super Pro, No Box, Street and Jr Dragster classes, plus TNT Friday nights.
faq: What classes does Twin City Raceway run?
Super Pro, No Box, Street and Jr Dragster. As advertised in September 2026, Super Pro pays $5,000 to win, No Box $2,000, Street $500 and Jr Dragster $500.
How much does it cost to race at Twin City Raceway?
Entry fees as advertised in September 2026 were $125 for Super Pro, $90 for No Box, and $40 for Street and Jr Dragster. Spectators are $15 and children $10. TNT sessions are $50.
Where is Twin City Raceway?
3695 Prairie Rd, Monroe, LA 71202, in north Louisiana.
Is Twin City Raceway the same as Twin City Motorsports Park?

Yes. Google lists the venue as Twin City Motorsports Park while the track's own Facebook page uses Twin City Raceway. Same place, 3695 Prairie Rd in Monroe, Louisiana, where Prairie Rd meets Highway 841.

tracks.name: Holiday Raceway
tracks.sanction: IHRA points races plus independent events
tracks.race_days: Open track and test and tune most Thursdays. Bracket racing on scheduled Saturdays, March through November.
tracks.notes:
A drag strip on Highway 11 in Woodstock, between Birmingham and Tuscaloosa, and one of the few tracks in this directory that publishes a full season schedule rather than announcing races week to week.

The regular pattern is open track and test and tune on Thursdays, with bracket racing on scheduled Saturdays running Pro, Footbrake and Junior Dragster. Several Saturdays carry raised purses: $5,000 to win in Pro or Footbrake, and $1,000 in Junior Dragster. A number of those count towards IHRA points.

The season runs late March through November and mixes bracket racing with bigger draws. The 2026 calendar included the Southeast Gassers Association over two days in May, a Streetcar Challenge in June, Street Outlaws small tire shootouts with Ryan Martin and Murder Nova across two days in August, King of the Beach in October, a 17th annual cruise-in with car, bike and truck shows in April, the Woodstock Music Festival in May, and a Thanksgiving Throwdown sound and audio competition in November.

The track closes for Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends. All dates are published as subject to change, so confirm before travelling.
tracks.answer: Holiday Raceway is a drag strip at 20105 Hwy 11 in Woodstock, Alabama, between Birmingham and Tuscaloosa. It runs open track and test and tune most Thursdays and bracket racing on scheduled Saturdays from March through November, with $5,000 purses in Pro and Footbrake and $1,000 in Junior Dragster.
faq: What days does Holiday Raceway race?
Open track and test and tune run most Thursdays. Bracket racing is on scheduled Saturdays, running Pro, Footbrake and Junior Dragster. The season runs late March through November.
How much can you win at Holiday Raceway?

Several Saturdays each season carry $5,000 to win in either Pro or Footbrake, and $1,000 to win in Junior Dragster. Other Saturdays run a regular purse. A number of the bigger races count towards IHRA points.
What big events does Holiday Raceway host?

The 2026 season included the Southeast Gassers Association, a Streetcar Challenge, Street Outlaws small tire shootouts with Ryan Martin and Murder Nova, King of the Beach, an annual cruise-in with car, bike and truck shows, the Woodstock Music Festival, and a Thanksgiving Throwdown sound and audio competition.
Where is Holiday Raceway?
20105 Hwy 11, Woodstock, AL 35188, between Birmingham and Tuscaloosa.

tracks.name: Montgomery International Dragway
tracks.race_days: Test and tune, bracket racing and big-money events across a published season. The 2026 calendar was released in January and revised in June.
tracks.notes:
An IHRA member track in Montgomery that publishes a full season calendar and revises it in writing, which makes it one of the easier tracks in this directory to plan around. The 2026 schedule was released in January and revised on 22 June.

It runs some of the biggest bracket money in the Southeast. The autumn calendar alone includes the Cap City $50K Bracket Race, the IHRA Bracket Finals, a $5,000 and $10,000 Footbrake Race with a double $2,000 Junior Dragster, the Gobble Wobble Thanksgiving Bracket and the World Footbrake Challenge.

The track also runs a heads-up index programme of six races, with 5.30, 6.00 and 7.00 index classes plus Mike Hill's 4.84 Series. Index rules as published allow a delay box and any tire size, on a .400 pro tree, with no throttle stop and no deep staging.

Other regular features are the Super 7 Series bracket races, Friday night slick-prepped test and tune sessions paired with a Top Eliminator bracket race, radial-prepped test and tune, and the Southern Outlaw Tour, which finishes its season here.

All dates are published as subject to change and the track has revised its calendar mid-season before, so confirm before travelling.

Venue update: the Great American event originally listed on Montgomery's 2026 calendar for Oct. 13-18 was officially moved to Gulfport Dragway on 17 September 2026. Gulf South Drags no longer lists that October event at Montgomery.
tracks.answer: Montgomery International Dragway is an IHRA-sanctioned quarter-mile drag strip at 2600 N Belt Drive in Montgomery, Alabama. It publishes a full season schedule and hosts major bracket events including the Cap City $50K, IHRA Bracket Finals and World Footbrake Challenge.
faq: What are the biggest races at Montgomery International Dragway?

The Cap City $50K Bracket Race, IHRA Bracket Finals and World Footbrake Challenge are among the largest remaining events on the 2026 calendar. The Great American event originally scheduled at Montgomery in October was moved to Gulfport Dragway on 17 September 2026.
Does Montgomery International Dragway run index racing?

Yes. It runs a heads-up index schedule of six races with 5.30, 6.00 and 7.00 index classes plus Mike Hill's 4.84 Series. Published rules allow a delay box and any tire size on a .400 pro tree, with no throttle stop and no deep staging.
Where is Montgomery International Dragway?
2600 N Belt Drive, Montgomery, AL 36110.

tracks.name: I-22 Motorsports Park
tracks.race_days: Bracket racing weekends plus invitational shootouts and multi-day bracket bashes. Announcements go out through Facebook.
tracks.notes:
An eighth-mile track in Eldridge, northwest Alabama. Confirmed active on 12 September 2026, with a 98 percent recommendation rate on its social page.

The track runs Super Pro, Footbrake and Jr Dragster, and puts up serious money for a track its size. Its Labor Day Weekend Bracket Bash in September 2026 paid $7,500 to win in Super Pro on the Saturday, $5,000 on the Sunday and $2,000 on the Friday, with entries of $175, $100 and $50 respectively and buybacks available. Footbrake paid $2,500, $1,500 and $1,000 across the same three days on entries of $80, $75 and $50. Payouts are posted as based on car counts — 75 cars for the Saturday Super Pro purse, 50 for the Sunday.

Weekend passes were offered at $250 single and $380 double for Super Pro, and $140 single and $250 double for Footbrake. Friday gates opened at 3pm with open time runs from 5pm to 7pm and racing to follow.

The track also runs invitational shootouts. Schedule announcements go out through Facebook rather than a website, so check there before travelling.
tracks.answer: I-22 Motorsports Park is an eighth-mile drag strip at 3928 Byler Rd in Eldridge, Alabama. It runs bracket racing in Super Pro, Footbrake and Jr Dragster, with multi-day bracket bashes paying up to $7,500 to win.
faq: What does I-22 Motorsports Park pay to win?

For its Labor Day Weekend Bracket Bash in September 2026, Super Pro paid $7,500 to win on Saturday, $5,000 on Sunday and $2,000 on Friday. Footbrake paid $2,500, $1,500 and $1,000 across the same three days. Purses are posted as based on car counts.
How much is entry at I-22 Motorsports Park?

For the 2026 Labor Day Bracket Bash, Super Pro entry was $175 Saturday, $100 Sunday and $50 Friday, with buybacks at $100, $60 and $40. Footbrake entry was $80, $75 and $50 with buybacks at $50, $40 and $30. Weekend passes were $250 single and $380 double for Super Pro.
Where is I-22 Motorsports Park?
3928 Byler Rd, Eldridge, AL 35554, in northwest Alabama.

tracks.name: Alabama International Dragway
tracks.race_days: Moonlight Madness every Friday night, 9pm to 1am. Additional events announced through the track’s Facebook page.
tracks.answer: Alabama International Dragway is a quarter-mile drag strip at 1245 Crump Road in Steele, Alabama, just off I-59 at exit 174. It runs Moonlight Madness every Friday night from 9pm to 1am.
tracks.notes:
A quarter-mile track in Steele, in northeast Alabama off Interstate 59 at exit 174. It opened in 1994.

By social following it is the largest track in this directory, with around 49,000 followers and an 88 percent recommendation rate across more than 1,700 reviews. It posts regularly and was confirmed active on 12 September 2026.

The signature programme is Moonlight Madness, run every Friday night from 9pm to 1am. That late slot is unusual and worth planning around if you are travelling.

This is the farthest track currently listed here, roughly 245 miles from Hattiesburg. It is included because it draws from a wide area and because racers from north Mississippi make the trip.
faq: What is Moonlight Madness at Alabama International Dragway?
A weekly Friday night programme running from 9pm to 1am at the track in Steele, Alabama. Check the track’s Facebook page for the current format and gate prices.
Where is Alabama International Dragway?
1245 Crump Road, Steele, AL 35987, just off Interstate 59 at exit 174.

camping.detail: Unconfirmed. Worth asking, given the late Friday finish.

tracks.name: Baileyton Goodtime Dragstrip
tracks.race_days: Saturday bracket racing. Gates 4pm, time runs 6pm. Announcements go out through the track’s Facebook page.
tracks.answer: Baileyton Goodtime Dragstrip is an eighth-mile track at 1582 Summit Rd in Baileyton, Alabama. It runs Saturday bracket racing with Footbrake paying $5,000 to win, Pro $1,000 and Jr Dragster $300 — guaranteed regardless of car count.
tracks.notes:
An eighth-mile track in Baileyton, north Alabama, known locally as the Goodtime. Confirmed active on 12 September 2026, with a 96 percent recommendation rate across 381 reviews.

The thing that sets Baileyton apart is that it guarantees its purses regardless of car count. Most tracks post payouts as based on a minimum number of entries, so a thin turnout means a smaller cheque. Baileyton pays what it advertises either way, in both classes.

As advertised for the September 2026 Saturday programme, Footbrake paid $5,000 to win with $500 to the runner-up, $100 to the semis and $50 to the quarter-finals, on a $100 single or $160 double entry with a $50 buyback. Pro paid $1,000 to win with $300 runner-up on a $60 entry and $40 buyback. Jr Dragster paid $300 to win with $50 runner-up on a $40 entry and $20 buyback.

Gates open at 4pm with time runs from 6pm. Spectators $10, children 12 and under free.

The track is listed on the WDRA member track list as Baileyton Drag Strip. Schedule announcements go out through Facebook.
faq: Does Baileyton Goodtime Dragstrip guarantee its purses?

Yes. The track advertises its payouts as guaranteed no matter the car count, in both Footbrake and Pro. That is unusual — most tracks post purses as based on a minimum number of entries, so a small turnout reduces the payout.
What does Baileyton pay to win?

As advertised in September 2026, Footbrake paid $5,000 to win with $500 runner-up, $100 to semis and $50 to quarter-finals. Pro paid $1,000 to win with $300 runner-up. Jr Dragster paid $300 to win with $50 runner-up.
What time do gates open at Baileyton Goodtime Dragstrip?
Gates open at 4pm with time runs from 6pm. Spectators are $10 and children 12 and under are free.
Where is Baileyton Goodtime Dragstrip?
1582 Summit Rd, Baileyton, AL 35019, in north Alabama.

One of the larger bracket purses on the Southeast calendar, run across four days.

Montgomery follows it the next week with the IHRA Bracket Finals, so racers travelling any distance often plan the two together.

events.name: $5,000 to Win Footbrake — Holiday Raceway
schedule: $5,000 to win in Footbrake, plus Pro and Junior Dragster
events.summary: Holiday Raceway runs $5,000 to win in Footbrake on Saturday 19 September 2026, with Pro and Junior Dragster also racing.
events.detail:
Footbrake classes are for cars without transbrakes or delay boxes — the driver launches off the footbrake, which puts more of the round on the driver and less on the electronics. A $5,000 purse is a significant draw for a Saturday bracket race.

Pro and Junior Dragster run the same day on a regular purse. Open track and test and tune runs the Thursday before, on 17 September.

Holiday Raceway publishes its dates as subject to change. Confirm with the track before travelling.

schedule: Super Saturday, presented by Flip Flop Promotions
events.summary: Super Saturday runs at No Problem Raceway Park on 19 September 2026, presented by Flip Flop Promotions.
events.detail:

faq: How many drag strips are there near the Mississippi Gulf Coast?
This directory tracks thirteen drag strips across Mississippi, Louisiana and Alabama. Ten are confirmed operating, two are permanently closed, and one has an uncertain future.
What is the closest drag strip to Hattiesburg, Mississippi?

Swamp Bottom Dragstrip in Columbia, about 34 miles away, which opened in September 2026. Hub City Dragway in Hattiesburg was closer at about 4 miles but is permanently closed. Gulfport Dragway is about 60 miles away and races Wednesday nights and weekends year-round.
What is the newest drag strip in Mississippi?
Swamp Bottom Dragstrip in Columbia, Mississippi, which opened on 5 September 2026. It is a quarter-mile concrete track and an NHRA member track in the South Central Division.
What is a dial-in in bracket racing?

A dial-in is the elapsed time a driver predicts their car will run, declared before a round. The slower car gets a head start equal to the difference between the two dial-ins, so both cars should theoretically reach the finish line together. Running quicker than your dial-in is a breakout and loses the round, so the skill is predicting your own car accurately.
Why does weather affect a drag racing dial-in?

Air density changes how much power an engine makes. Temperature, humidity and barometric pressure combine into density altitude, and a car that runs 12.50 in cool morning air may run 12.65 in hot afternoon air. Racers track density altitude against past runs to predict what the car will do in current conditions.
What is the difference between a quarter-mile and an eighth-mile track?

A quarter-mile track measures 1,320 feet from the starting line to the finish; an eighth-mile measures 660 feet. Many tracks have both, and eighth-mile racing has become more common because it is easier on equipment and needs less shutdown area.
Can you camp or park an RV at drag strips on the Mississippi Gulf Coast?

Most tracks in this region allow some form of overnight pit parking, but very few publish the details — whether hookups are available, what they cost, or whether you need to book. We are collecting this track by track and marking it unconfirmed until we have it direct from the track.
What bracket racing series run on the Mississippi Gulf Coast?

The main ones are BTE King of the Coast, the IHRA Sportsman Series at IHRA member tracks like Gulfport Dragway, and the NHRA Summit Racing E.T. Series at NHRA member tracks like Swamp Bottom Dragstrip. The Southeast Gassers Association also visits the region for its Gulf Coast Nationals.

series.name: BTE King of the Coast Bracket Racing Series
series.answer: BTE King of the Coast is an independent bracket racing series running on the Mississippi Gulf Coast. It has around 7,300 followers on Facebook and is followed by Gulfport Dragway.
series.notes:
A multi-race bracket series rather than a single track's weekly program. Series like this are the hardest thing to follow in regional drag racing: the schedule lives across several tracks' Facebook pages and is rarely published in one place.

We have not yet confirmed the full 2026 schedule or the complete list of host tracks. If you run or race this series, send us the schedule and we will publish it.

series.name: Southeast Gassers Association
series.answer: The Southeast Gassers Association runs front-engine, straight-axle gassers to a 1960s period rulebook — no electronics, no delay boxes, flag starts. It races at tracks across the Southeast and holds its Gulf Coast Nationals at Gulfport Dragway.
series.notes:
SEGA is a throwback series and one of the bigger crowd draws at any track it visits. Cars run to a period rulebook, which rules out the electronics that dominate modern bracket racing.

The series normally runs one race per weekend, with a relaxed test and tune on Friday evening. The 2026 Gulf Coast Nationals at Gulfport is a double feature, with full competition both Friday and Saturday.

series.name: IHRA Sportsman Series
series.region: National, with Gulf Coast member tracks
series.answer: The IHRA Sportsman Series is the International Hot Rod Association's bracket racing programme for member tracks. Gulfport Dragway runs an IHRA Track Championship Series, and Hub City Dragway has historically run IHRA ET bracket racing.
series.notes:
IHRA member tracks run their own points programmes under the series banner, with track champions advancing to larger events. Gulfport's version includes the Summer Iron Man Challenge.

Check with the individual track for the current points schedule — these change from season to season and are not published centrally.

series.name: NHRA Summit Racing Equipment E.T. Series
series.answer: The NHRA Summit Racing Equipment E.T. Series presented by Hoosier is NHRA's bracket racing programme for member tracks. Swamp Bottom Dragstrip is eligible to run it as a new South Central Division member track.
series.notes:
Member tracks run weekly and points events under the series banner, with champions advancing to divisional and national competition. NHRA's South Central Division covers Mississippi, Louisiana, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Texas.

Swamp Bottom joined the Member Track Network in July 2026, which also makes it eligible for the Summit Jr. Drag Racing League, NHRA Street Legal, Jr. Street and specialty events such as Summit King of the Track. Its first season schedule has not been published yet.

series.name: Busch Light King of the Mountain
series.answer: Busch Light King of the Mountain is Gulfport Dragway's weekly Wednesday night programme, running alongside grudge racing and test and tune.
series.notes: Gulfport publishes results from each Wednesday night on its own website. Gates open at 6pm, weather permitting, and the programme runs from roughly February through December.

series.name: Southern Outlaw Tour
series.answer: The Southern Outlaw Tour is a four-race drag racing series running at Montgomery International Dragway, Gulfport Dragway and Alabama International Dragway in Steele, with the finale back at Montgomery.
series.notes:
A four-race series announced for 2026, run in partnership between Montgomery International Dragway and DragCoverage. Montgomery's schedule names TJ Pruitt and DragCoverage as partners on the tour.

The rounds run at Montgomery International Dragway, Gulfport Dragway, Alabama International Dragway in Steele for its Night of Fire, and the finale back at Montgomery. Montgomery's published calendar shows finale qualifying with ProMods and 5.30, 6.00 and 7.00 index classes plus a $5,000 bracket race, with any tire size allowed, followed by the main event the next day.

Series like this are the hardest thing to follow in regional drag racing. The schedule lives across three tracks' Facebook pages and nowhere else. If you have the full round-by-round calendar, send it over and we will publish it.
